title: subpoena-witness network line
description: One line of subpoena-witness -net-out output: one outbound connection attempt as the kernel saw it, or a record that opens or closes a capture window. A line with a record field is a record; any other line is an attempt. The records are those of witness-event.schema.json. See docs/ports.md (W). Readers ignore fields they do not know; existing fields keep their name and meaning.

time.description: When the attempt was seen, or the record written (RFC 3339, UTC).

op.description: connect: connect() on an inet socket. sendmsg: a send with an explicit destination (sendto, sendmsg, sendmmsg). Readers keep an op they do not know.

protocol.description: tcp, udp, icmp, icmpv6, sctp, mptcp, or the IP protocol number.

dest.description: The destination address and port: ip:port, [ip]:port for IPv6, an IPv4-mapped address in its IPv4 form, no zone. A reader refuses any other form.

pid.description: PID in the witness's PID namespace; 0 when the process is not visible there.

host_pid.description: PID in the initial PID namespace.

comm.description: Kernel task name, at most 15 bytes.

sock_type.description: The socket type: 1 SOCK_STREAM, 2 SOCK_DGRAM, 3 SOCK_RAW, ...

cgroup.description: cgroup path without the hierarchy root, root-most first, at most 8 elements, such as subpoena/<trace id>.

trace_id.description: The session's trace ID, read from its cgroup name. Present only for attempts from inside a session cgroup.

attribution.description: How the attempt was tied to trace_id. Present exactly when trace_id is.

record.description: start: the witness is attached and capturing. stop: it has stopped; healthy says whether the capture between start and stop is complete.

healthy.description: On a stop record: true only if no kernel events were lost and no read or write failed.

error.description: On an unhealthy stop record: what went wrong.
